FROMLIST: soc: mediatek: add new flow for mtcmos power. Both MT8183 & MT6765 add more bus protect node than previous project, therefore we add two more register for setup bus protect, which reside at INFRA_CFG & SMI_COMMON. With the following change 1. bus protect need not only infracfg but smi_common registers involved to setup. Therefore we add a set/clr APIs with more customize arguments. The second change is that we also add subsys CG control flow before/after the bus protect/sram control, due to bus protect need SMI bus relative CGs enable to feed-back its ack, and some master's sram control need CG enable to on/off its resource sequentially. With the following change 1. turn on subsys CG before sram pwron and release bus protect. 2. turn off subsys CG after the process of set bus protect/receive ack/disable sram. The last change is for some power domains like vpu_core on MT8183 whose sram need to do clock and internal isolation while power on/off sram. We add a flag "sram_iso_ctrl" in scp_domain_data to judge if we need to do the extra sram isolation control or not. BACKPORT: mac80211: call drv_stop only if driver is started If drv_start() fails during hw_restart, all the running interfaces are being closed/stopped, which results in drv_stop() being called, although the driver was never started successfully. This might cause drivers to perform operations on uninitialized memory (as they assume it was initialized on drv_start) Consider the local->started flag, and call the driver's stop() op only if drv_start() succeeded before. Move drv_start() and drv_stop() to driver-ops.c, as they are no longer simple wrappers. shill: wifi: Stop assuming kFailureOutOfRange as default disconnect reason Currently, unexpected wifi disconnects are assumed to either be due to bad credentials or to the AP being out of range. This change uses disconnect reasons and signal strength in order to determine the the proper disconnect reason to return. One potential pitfall with the current logic is that SuspectOutOfRange uses the last known BSS signal strength, which it polls from the AP every 20 seconds. A signal strength below the threshold will lead to a suspected out of range if no other reason presents itself. Thus it is possible for a STA to move quickly away from the AP, such that the last known signal strength is above the threshold, leading shill to determine that the disconnect was caused due to unknown reasons instead of an out of range error.
